triggers: Your agent reads channel history: a new unlisted app of your own gets conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request/minute and 15 objects per call until it is approved for the Slack Marketplace. Check this before leaving managed auth.
You need user-facing branding in the "Add to Slack" consent screen or your own bot name and icon (inferred from the generic branding trigger).
ownApp.notes: Composio lists Slack as a Composio-managed OAuth toolkit. We did not verify whether Composio's managed app is Marketplace-listed, so we can't say whether it avoids the non-Marketplace throttle. Your own app is free and self-serve, but scale depends on Marketplace approval. Copy the redirect URL from the Composio dashboard (Create Auth Config); Slack requires HTTPS.

verdict.summary: Minutes to build, weeks to months to scale. Unlisted apps work in other workspaces, but history reads are throttled to 1 request/minute until Marketplace approval: up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks, and you need 10 active installs first.

milestones.definition: The app is installed in its own development workspace and API calls work.

limitsUntilNext.value: By default a new app installs only in its associated workspace.

sources.quote: By default, a newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace as mentioned above.

milestones.definition: Other workspaces can install the app through unlisted distribution.

limitsUntilNext.value: Commercially distributed apps created after 2025-05-29 that are not Marketplace-approved: conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request.

sources.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.

limitsUntilNext.value: Slack positions unlisted distribution for pilots; commercial apps should be submitted to the Marketplace.

sources.quote: Distributing your unlisted app is perfect for when you want to test out your app by running a pilot for early customers; however, apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

milestones.definition: Approved for the Slack Marketplace, which lifts the history throttle for any workspace.

limitsUntilNext.value: Review is "up to" 10 business days (preliminary) plus "up to" 10 weeks (functional) for new apps; Slack won't expedite. 84 days is the sum of the two upper bounds and excludes time spent fixing feedback or reaching 10 installs.

sources.quote: Currently, the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days to receive feedback, while the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes.

gates.name: Non-Marketplace commercial app rate limit (1 req/min, 15 objects on conversations.history/replies)

duration.value: Lasts until the app is approved for the Slack Marketplace. Internal customer-built apps are not affected.

sources.quote: This change will not impact Marketplace apps.

duration.value: Up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks for the functional review (6 weeks for resubmissions).

sources.quote: We are unable to skip or accelerate the review process in order to coordinate with your launch.

cost.value: Prerequisite: at least 10 installations on active workspaces, maintained for the whole review.

sources.quote: Your app needs to stay at 10 or more installed workspaces throughout the entire duration of the review .

cost.note: No fee found. The cost here is the install prerequisite.

requirements.label: A Slack workspace where you can install apps
requirements.detail: Development happens in the app's associated workspace.

requirements.label: HTTPS redirect URL
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS and match, or be a subdirectory of, a Redirect URL configured in App Management. Use the Composio dashboard's URL.

requirements.label: 10 active workspace installs
requirements.detail: Needed to submit to the Marketplace, and must hold through the whole review, while you are still throttled.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.whyNeeded: Read messages in public channels the app is in (conversations.history / replies).
scopes.reviewTrigger: No per-scope review, but the history methods are throttled for unlisted commercial apps; the Marketplace review covers all requested scopes.
scopes.justificationDraft: The agent summarizes threads in channels the user has added it to.

scopes.name: chat:write
scopes.reviewTrigger: Reviewed only as part of a Marketplace submission.

steps.title: Check whether the throttle hits your agent
actions: List the Web API methods the agent calls. If it uses conversations.history or conversations.replies across many workspaces, plan for the Marketplace.
If only one customer uses it, consider an internal app built in their workspace (not throttled).
steps.doneWhen: You know whether you need the Marketplace path.

steps.title: Create the app from a manifest
actions: api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest.
Paste a manifest with bot scopes and the HTTPS redirect URL.
steps.doneWhen: A bot token works in your workspace.

steps.title: Enable distribution and wire Composio
actions: Decide on token rotation now: once on it can't be turned off, and access tokens then expire every 12 hours.
Copy client ID and secret into a Composio auth config.
steps.doneWhen: A second workspace can install via your auth config.

steps.title: Reach 10 installs and submit to the Marketplace
actions: Recruit at least 10 active workspaces and keep them installed.
Prepare listing copy, privacy policy and support pages; submit and answer reviewer feedback.
steps.doneWhen: The app is approved for the Slack Marketplace.

redirectUris.value: HTTPS only; the redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL.

sources.quote: Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management .

pkce.value: Supported, but enabling it marks the app as a public client, which can't be undone without Slack support. Server-side agents usually don't need it.

sources.quote: Enabling PKCE marks your app as a public client, which is is a one-way operation.

tokenLifetime.value: Without token rotation, access tokens never expire. With rotation they expire every 12 hours.

sources.quote: Without token rotation, the access token never expires.

refresh.value: Token rotation is opt-in and can't be turned off once enabled.

sources.quote: Token rotation may not be turned off once it's turned on

rateLimits.value: Unlisted commercial apps: conversations.history/replies at 1 request/minute and 15 objects (Tier 1 instead of Tier 3).

sources.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.

rateLimits.value: Other Web API methods follow per-method tiers (Tier 1: 1+ per minute … Tier 3: 50+ per minute).

blockers.description: Unlisted commercial apps read channel history at 1 request/minute and 15 objects per call. An agent that summarizes channels is effectively unusable at scale.
blockers.workaround: Pilot with few workspaces, or have a single customer build an internal app (not throttled). The real fix is Marketplace approval.

blockers.description: The Marketplace needs 10 active installs held through the whole review, which you must recruit while still throttled.
blockers.workaround: Line up design partners before submitting.

blockers.description: Marketplace review takes up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks, and Slack won't accelerate it.
blockers.workaround: Submit as early as possible; keep the reviewer test workspace working.

agentTasks: Generate the app manifest with the minimum bot scopes.
Audit which API methods the agent calls and flag throttled ones.
Draft Marketplace listing copy and reviewer test instructions.
humanTasks: Install the app as a workspace admin.
Recruit and retain 10 active workspace installs.
Submit to the Marketplace and respond to reviewer feedback.

probes.observed: OIDC discovery for Sign in with Slack (authorization_endpoint https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize). The app OAuth v2 flow uses slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize instead.
Authorize endpoint is live; unauthenticated requests go to workspace sign-in before the client_id is validated. The first request (without tracked=1) returned 200 with a JS redirect.

unknowns: Whether Composio's managed Slack app is Marketplace-listed (and so exempt from the history throttle).

Research.md reported (secondary) that the throttle was extended to existing installs from 2026-03-03. The official 2025-05-29 entry and its 2025-06-03 clarification (internal customer-built apps keep existing limits) say nothing about such an extension; we found no official confirmation.
Marketplace minimum review time: Slack publishes only upper bounds.
Whether a Marketplace listing has any fee (none found).

evidence.claim: New apps install only in their associated workspace by default; unlisted distribution is meant for pilots.
evidence.quote: By default, a newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace as mentioned above.

evidence.claim: Non-Marketplace commercial apps get 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history/replies.
evidence.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.

evidence.claim: Marketplace review: up to 10 business days preliminary, up to 10 weeks functional; no acceleration.
evidence.quote: Currently, the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days to receive feedback, while the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes.

evidence.claim: Marketplace submissions need at least 10 active workspace installs, held through review.
evidence.quote: As of July 2026, we require that apps submitting to the Slack Marketplace have at least 10 installations on active workspaces, up from the temporary lower threshold.

evidence.claim: With token rotation, access tokens expire every 12 hours; rotation can't be turned off.
evidence.quote: With token rotation, it expires every 12 hours.

evidence.claim: Enabling PKCE makes the app a public client, one-way.
evidence.quote: It cannot be disabled without contacting Slack support.

evidence.claim: Internal customer-built apps keep their existing rate limits.
evidence.quote: Any internal customer-built apps will maintain their existing rate limits and will not be subject to the new posted limits.

evidence.claim: slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize is live and routes unauthenticated users to workspace sign-in.

corrections.before: Unlisted distribution is enough for production.
corrections.after: Unlisted commercial apps get 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history/replies; lifting that needs Marketplace approval, which needs 10 active installs and up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks.
corrections.reason: Slack's 2025-05-29 rate-limit change and the July 2026 install requirement.
